# Third-party notices

## Voice Lab model and calibration data

WeSpeaker ResNet34-LM weights (VoxCeleb2 Dev), official WeSpeaker ONNX export at Hugging Face revision `f0c48c298fd835726c27956a5d617bad7115627e`: CC BY 4.0, per the official model card and WeSpeaker pretrained-model licence statement. Attribution: WeSpeaker project; Hongji Wang et al., “WeSpeaker: A research and production oriented speaker embedding learning toolkit,” ICASSP 2023. The weights are downloaded on request, unmodified, and never bundled. The toolkit itself is Apache-2.0 (full text below).

LibriSpeech test-clean excerpts: LibriSpeech (c) 2014 Vassil Panayotov, CC BY 4.0. Source: `https://www.openslr.org/resources/12/test-clean.tar.gz`, SHA-256 `39fde525e59672dc6d1551919b1478f724438a95aa55f874b576be21967e6c23`. Four six-second speech excerpts in `shared/fixtures/voice-lab/speaker/` were decoded from FLAC to mono 16 kHz PCM16 WAV and truncated. Four additional renders resample two of those excerpts to 48 kHz and 44.1 kHz. These are modifications; see that folder’s README for utterance IDs and books. Neither corpus nor model is endorsed by VoxClip or its original authors.

VoxClip is MIT-licensed (see `LICENSE`). It bundles or links the third-party components below, each under its own licence. This is the single notices file: `bundle.sh` copies it into `VoxClip.app/Contents/Resources/` and the Windows release copies it into the install folder (doc/release.md). Every new dependency, font, data file or model adds its section here in the same change, with the exact licence text from the pinned package.

Sections: Fonts; Data (Unicode Character Database); Application components (macOS, Windows); Models (downloaded at the user's request, never bundled); licence texts.

## Windows installer prerequisite

VoxClip does not bundle or redistribute the Microsoft Visual C++ runtime. Windows Setup uses Velopack's `vcredist145-x64` or `vcredist145-arm64` prerequisite to install Microsoft's official Visual C++ 2015-2026 Redistributable package under Microsoft's terms. Microsoft supplies the package and its licence; its DLLs are not copied into VoxClip. Installer verification requires runtime version 14.44 or newer for Whisper.net's native libraries. Velopack 1.2.161's vcredist145 prerequisite requires at least 14.50, so an older installation is upgraded rather than satisfying Setup below the release gate.

## Fonts

Caption fonts and emoji images in `shared/fonts/`, bundled unmodified with both apps (doc/spec/captions.md section 4). Each family's licence file ships next to its fonts. Source URLs are pinned to the commit the files were taken from; `shared/fonts/fonts.json` records the sha256 of every file.

## Data

### Unicode Character Database

- Files: `shared/caption-styles/casemap.json`, derived from `UnicodeData.txt` 16.0.0 (simple case mappings) by `tools/captions/build_casemap.py`; `shared/data/share-text.json`, whose emoji table is derived from `emoji-data.txt` 15.1.0 (Emoji_Presentation ranges) by `shared/fixtures/share/generate_share_cases.py`; both shipped with both apps.

## Application components

Libraries linked into or shipped with the apps. SwiftPM, NuGet, the .NET SDK runtime packs, and `apps/windows/build/ffmpeg.json` determine the versions. Build-only SDK tools and components already installed with Windows are excluded from the shipped-component list.

### macOS

| Component | Use | Licence |
|---|---|---|
| whisper.cpp / ggml (xcframework, release b5454) | on-device transcription | MIT (The ggml authors) |
| ONNX Runtime SwiftPM 1.19.2 (`bbc428e168a0374eb7d0503cdb7c73fdc1d99751`) | CPU-only own-voice embeddings; static Apple runtime | MIT (Microsoft Corporation); complete upstream third-party notices below |
| swift-argument-parser 1.8.2 (`6a52f3251125d74daf04fcbd5e6f08a75d074382`) | `voxclip-cli` argument parsing | Apache-2.0 (text above), with runtime library exception below |
#### ONNX Runtime SwiftPM 1.19.2

The official `microsoft/onnxruntime-swift-package-manager` package is pinned to `v1.19.2`, commit `bbc428e168a0374eb7d0503cdb7c73fdc1d99751`. The binary archive `https://download.onnxruntime.ai/pod-archive-onnxruntime-c-1.19.2.zip` has SHA-256 `28787ee2f966a2c47eb293322c733c5dc4b5e3327cec321c1fe31a7c698edf68`. No Extensions product or extra execution provider is selected. The Apple CPU build uses MLAS, not Intel MKL; the all-platform upstream notices below do not authorize adding MKL to the Mac app.

TVM Contributors
================
TVM adopts the Apache style model and governs by merit. We believe that it is important to create an inclusive community where everyone can use,
contribute to, and influence the direction of the project. We actively invite contributors who have earned the merit to be part of the development community.

See the [community structure document](http://docs.tvm.ai/contribute/community.html) for the explanation of community structure and contribution guidelines.

SQLite Is Public Domain

All of the code and documentation in SQLite has been dedicated to the public
domain by the authors. All code authors, and representatives of the companies
they work for, have signed affidavits dedicating their contributions to the
public domain and originals of those signed affidavits are stored in a firesafe
at the main offices of Hwaci. Anyone is free to copy, modify, publish, use,
compile, sell, or distribute the original SQLite code, either in source code
form or as a compiled binary, for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial,
and by any means.

The previous paragraph applies to the deliverable code and documentation in
SQLite - those parts of the SQLite library that you actually bundle and ship
with a larger application. Some scripts used as part of the build process (for
example the "configure" scripts generated by autoconf) might fall under other
open-source licenses. Nothing from these build scripts ever reaches the final
deliverable SQLite library, however, and so the licenses associated with those
scripts should not be a factor in assessing your rights to copy and use the
SQLite library.

All of the deliverable code in SQLite has been written from scratch. No code
has been taken from other projects or from the open internet. Every line of
code can be traced back to its original author, and all of those authors have
public domain dedications on file. So the SQLite code base is clean and is
uncontaminated with licensed code from other projects.

| nv-codec-headers, AMF headers, libvpl dispatcher | Windows vendor encoding interfaces; no GPU driver is bundled | MIT; exact source pins and notices below |

`Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools` 10.0.28000.2705 and its MSIX build-tools dependency are build inputs with `PrivateAssets=all`; their SDK terms do not describe an app redistributable. `SkiaSharp.NativeAssets.macOS`, `HarfBuzzSharp.NativeAssets.macOS`, and `Whisper.net.Runtime.Metal` are resolved for cross-platform development but their macOS binaries do not ship in the Windows package. The Windows App SDK ML 2.1.94, Microsoft.Windows.AI.MachineLearning 2.1.74, AI 2.5.5, Search 2.5.5 and Widgets 2.0.5 packages that `Microsoft.WindowsAppSDK` 2.5.1 also resolves are excluded with `ExcludeAssets="all"`: none of their files or WinRT registrations ship, so Windows ML's ONNX Runtime and DirectML are not distributed and the only `onnxruntime.dll` is the pinned Microsoft.ML.OnnxRuntime 1.19.2 one. Windows-provided DirectX, audio, and OS APIs are not copied from NuGet. The WebView2 loader DLL is copied from NuGet; the WebView2 browser runtime is installed separately. The package notices below reproduce the suppliers' complete notice files; a notice file can describe more upstream components than the selected runtime DLLs contain.

### Velopack 1.2.161 Windows Setup, Update and stub payloads

The `vpk` 1.2.161 NuGet package (`ac9be73846d9a7a76483f8684abd1503cd50703b992727429dcdc045589c5e08` SHA-256) contains `vendor/setup_{x64,arm64}.exe`, `update_{x64,arm64}.exe` and `stub_{x64,arm64}.exe`. Its `vpk.nuspec` pins source commit `92d6a1c91716729d449034df5c50307dcce39493`. These are inputs to the generated installer, packaged `Squirrel.exe` (installed as `Update.exe`), and execution stub; the packer changes resources, appends the package to Setup, and signs the files. The supplier’s `vendor/THIRD_PARTY_NOTICES.md` covers build tools, not this Rust payload. The source files and crates below provide additional notices for the selected Windows target package graph; the graph can include build-time crates and does not prove that every crate is linked into each final executable. The Apache 2.0 text for the Google fastzip files is also reproduced in the Fonts section above.

#### Other selected Windows Rust crate licence texts

The following package identities come from the pinned `Cargo.lock` normal-dependency graph for `velopack_bins` on the two Windows targets, excluding proc-macro packages and their build-only subtrees. This is a conservative package graph, not a final binary link map. The pinned MIT text is selected where the source offers it, otherwise the available permissive licence text from that source is reproduced. Identical licence files are printed once and referenced by SHA-256 prefix. SQLite Is Public Domain

All of the code and documentation in SQLite has been dedicated to the public
domain by the authors. All code authors, and representatives of the companies
they work for, have signed affidavits dedicating their contributions to the
public domain and originals of those signed affidavits are stored in a firesafe
at the main offices of Hwaci. Anyone is free to copy, modify, publish, use,
compile, sell, or distribute the original SQLite code, either in source code
form or as a compiled binary, for any purpose, commercial or non-commercial,
and by any means.

The previous paragraph applies to the deliverable code and documentation in
SQLite - those parts of the SQLite library that you actually bundle and ship
with a larger application. Some scripts used as part of the build process (for
example the "configure" scripts generated by autoconf) might fall under other
open-source licenses. Nothing from these build scripts ever reaches the final
deliverable SQLite library, however, and so the licenses associated with those
scripts should not be a factor in assessing your rights to copy and use the
SQLite library.

All of the deliverable code in SQLite has been written from scratch. No code
has been taken from other projects or from the open internet. Every line of
code can be traced back to its original author, and all of those authors have
public domain dedications on file. So the SQLite code base is clean and is
uncontaminated with licensed code from other projects.

### Windows SDK .NET projection 10.0.26100.57 licence terms

The observed restore with .NET SDK 10.0.102 selects the `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.NET.Ref` 10.0.26100.57 targeting and runtime pack for the App's `net10.0-windows10.0.26100.0` build. This pack is SDK-selected, not explicitly pinned; the release SDK's actual pack must be checked before publication. Its `data/RuntimeList.xml` lists two files that ship with the App:

| File | Version | SHA-256 in the pack |
|---|---|---|
| `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.NET.dll` (Windows SDK for .NET 8) | 10.0.26100.55 (product version `10.0.26100.55+7e1ba99b2f0c1ea5311dcb3acfe20a75335efd6e`) | `c633ab241cd09846c2aa409f0bee2026962610404a7bf132c75cbd66b0e5a9f4` |
| `WinRT.Runtime.dll` (C#/WinRT Runtime) | 2.2.0.48161 (product version `2.2.0.48161+8649ee3eeb2445ca2a36d80d878ef60b96a6c65d`) | `bcf3a14e8712a90837fc5c0d8c8a24696af2bd7f74e9767597ec81ededfb23db` |

Both files carry `Copyright (c) Microsoft Corporation. All rights reserved.` The pack contains no licence file: its NuGet metadata requires licence acceptance and names the terms only by `https://aka.ms/WinSDKLicenseURL`. The text below is the exact `sdk_license.txt` from `Microsoft.Windows.SDK.BuildTools.MSIX` 1.7.251221100 (SHA-256 `a7a5c7e7ff998558983d6aca2702117c328aeb0c6404d298cb275f5623c6fd13`), the Windows SDK licence file in the same restore graph, after newline normalization.

Most files in FFmpeg are under the GNU Lesser General Public License version 2.1

Some optional parts of FFmpeg are licensed under the GNU General Public License

these parts are used by default, you have to explicitly pass `--enable-gpl` to
configure to activate them. In this case, FFmpeg's license changes to GPL v2+.

Specifically, the GPL parts of FFmpeg are:

- optional x86 optimization in the files

## External libraries

FFmpeg can be combined with a number of external libraries, which sometimes
affect the licensing of binaries resulting from the combination.

### Compatible libraries

The following libraries are under GPL version 2:
- avisynth
- frei0r
- libcdio
- libdavs2
- librubberband
- libvidstab
- libx264
- libx265
- libxavs
- libxavs2
- libxvid

When combining them with FFmpeg, FFmpeg needs to be licensed as GPL as well by
passing `--enable-gpl` to configure.

The following libraries are under LGPL version 3:
- gmp
- libaribb24
- liblensfun

When combining them with FFmpeg, use the configure option `--enable-version3` to
upgrade FFmpeg to the LGPL v3.

The VMAF, mbedTLS, RK MPI, OpenCORE and VisualOn libraries are under the Apache License
2.0. That license is incompatible with the LGPL v2.1 and the GPL v2, but not with
version 3 of those licenses. So to combine these libraries with FFmpeg, the
license version needs to be upgraded by passing `--enable-version3` to configure.

The smbclient library is under the GPL v3, to combine it with FFmpeg,
the options `--enable-gpl` and `--enable-version3` have to be passed to
configure to upgrade FFmpeg to the GPL v3.

### Incompatible libraries

There are certain libraries you can combine with FFmpeg whose licenses are not
compatible with the GPL and/or the LGPL. If you wish to enable these
libraries, even in circumstances that their license may be incompatible, pass
`--enable-nonfree` to configure. This will cause the resulting binary to be
unredistributable.

The Fraunhofer FDK AAC and OpenSSL libraries are under licenses which are
incompatible with the GPLv2 and v3. To the best of our knowledge, they are
compatible with the LGPL.

 * documentation must state that "this software is based in part on the work
 * of the Independent JPEG Group".
 * (3) Permission for use of this software is granted only if the user accepts
 * full responsibility for any undesirable consequences; the authors accept
 * NO LIABILITY for damages of any kind.
 *
 * These conditions apply to any software derived from or based on the IJG
 * code, not just to the unmodified library.  If you use our work, you ought
 * to acknowledge us.
 *
 * Permission is NOT granted for the use of any IJG author's name or company
 * name in advertising or publicity relating to this software or products
 * derived from it.  This software may be referred to only as "the Independent
 * JPEG Group's software".
 *
 * We specifically permit and encourage the use of this software as the basis
 * of commercial products, provided that all warranty or liability claims are
 * assumed by the product vendor.
 *
 * This file contains a fast, not so accurate integer implementation of the
 * forward DCT (Discrete Cosine Transform).
 *
 * A 2-D DCT can be done by 1-D DCT on each row followed by 1-D DCT
 * on each column.  Direct algorithms are also available, but they are
 * much more complex and seem not to be any faster when reduced to code.
 *
 * This implementation is based on Arai, Agui, and Nakajima's algorithm for
 * scaled DCT.  Their original paper (Trans. IEICE E-71(11):1095) is in
 * Japanese, but the algorithm is described in the Pennebaker & Mitchell
 * JPEG textbook (see REFERENCES section in file README).  The following code
 * is based directly on figure 4-8 in P&M.
 * While an 8-point DCT cannot be done in less than 11 multiplies, it is
 * possible to arrange the computation so that many of the multiplies are
 * simple scalings of the final outputs.  These multiplies can then be
 * folded into the multiplications or divisions by the JPEG quantization
 * table entries.  The AA&N method leaves only 5 multiplies and 29 adds
 * to be done in the DCT itself.
 * The primary disadvantage of this method is that with fixed-point math,
 * accuracy is lost due to imprecise representation of the scaled
 * quantization values.  The smaller the quantization table entry, the less
 * precise the scaled value, so this implementation does worse with high-
 * quality-setting files than with low-quality ones.
 */

 * JPEG Group's software".

 * We specifically permit and encourage the use of this software as the basis
 * of commercial products, provided that all warranty or liability claims are
 * assumed by the product vendor.
 *
 * This file contains the basic inverse-DCT transformation subroutine.
 *
 * This implementation is based on an algorithm described in
 *   C. Loeffler, A. Ligtenberg and G. Moschytz, "Practical Fast 1-D DCT
 *   Algorithms with 11 Multiplications", Proc. Int'l. Conf. on Acoustics,
 *   Speech, and Signal Processing 1989 (ICASSP '89), pp. 988-991.
 * The primary algorithm described there uses 11 multiplies and 29 adds.
 * We use their alternate method with 12 multiplies and 32 adds.
 * The advantage of this method is that no data path contains more than one
 * multiplication; this allows a very simple and accurate implementation in
 * scaled fixed-point arithmetic, with a minimal number of shifts.
 *
 * I've made lots of modifications to attempt to take advantage of the
 * sparse nature of the DCT matrices we're getting.  Although the logic
 * is cumbersome, it's straightforward and the resulting code is much
 * faster.
 *
 * A better way to do this would be to pass in the DCT block as a sparse
 * matrix, perhaps with the difference cases encoded.
 */

## Pinned Windows FFmpeg dependencies

The self-built minimal FFmpeg uses the pins in `tools/ffmpeg-build/sources.json` and the recipe at the release BUILD_COMMIT. Exact pinned-package notices follow. zimg is not included; the existing swscale HDR fallback avoids its unapproved WTFPL-2 licence. Ninja and Meson are pinned build-only host tools, not linked DLL dependencies.

## Models

Transcription models are downloaded from their publishers only when the user asks, after a confirmation that names the publisher and licence, and are never bundled. Their licence, attribution and citation come from `shared/catalog/transcription-models.json` and are shown in About → Licences for every installed model (doc/spec/transcription.md section 12.4). All v1 models are MIT: the TalTech Estonian Whisper fine-tune and its GGML conversions, OpenAI Whisper large-v3-turbo, small.en and base.en GGML files, and Silero VAD.
